items.claim: "Moss (Bryophyta), Polytrichopsida, Polytrichaceae"; "basalmost moss clade with hydroids"; bryophytes "sister to tracheophytes".
items.section: Front matter: lineage and placement_confidence
items.evidence: Ligrone identifies Polytrichopsida as the earliest-diverging hydroid-bearing clade; Harris supports monophyletic bryophytes sister to tracheophytes.
items.source: [Ligrone et al. 2012](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/221853422_Major_transitions_in_the_evolution_of_early_land_plants_a_bryological_perspective), full text; [Harris et al. 2022](https://bpb-eu-w2.wpmucdn.com/blogs.bristol.ac.uk/dist/3/589/files/2022/09/Harris_et_al_2022.pdf), full text.

items.claim: "No Polytrichopsida fossil, and no unequivocal moss fossil" in the window; oldest claimed unequivocal mosses are "Mississippian (late Visean)".
items.section: Front matter: range.notes
items.evidence: Hübers and Kerp describe fragmentary late Visean mosses; Ignatov and Maslova question their identification and the earlier proposed records.
items.source: [Hübers and Kerp 2012](https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/gsa/geology/article-abstract/40/8/755/131004/Oldest-known-mosses-discovered-in-Mississippian?redirectedFrom=fulltext), abstract only; [Ignatov and Maslova 2021](https://mapress.com/bde/article/download/bde.43.1.7/44441), indexed full-text passages; PDF retrieval exceeded the tool's size limit.

items.claim: "Meantoinea alophosioides, Early Cretaceous of Vancouver Island, a hard minimum age of 136 Ma for the family".
items.section: Front matter: range.notes
items.evidence: Five permineralised gametophytes come from Valanginian deposits dated using oxygen-isotope analyses; the authors explicitly propose a 136 Ma family minimum.
items.source: [Bippus et al. 2017](https://mihaibotany.online/pdf/BippusEtAl2017.pdf), full text.

items.claim: "Eopolytrichum antiquum, early Campanian of Georgia, USA, about 80 Ma"; "nested within Polytrichum".
items.section: Front matter: range.notes; Age and distribution
items.evidence: Konopka reports early Campanian fossils approximately 80 Ma old; Bippus places Eopolytrichum with P. commune and P. piliferum.
items.source: [Konopka et al. 1997](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/297459), publisher abstract; [Bippus et al. 2018](https://ri.conicet.gov.ar/bitstream/handle/11336/98858/CONICET_Digital_Nro.71ec348b-d4e4-4c9c-810f-af678b0a2825_A.pdf?isAllowed=n&sequence=2), full text.

items.claim: "Platteville Formation, Wisconsin, 455-454 Ma", "Sandbian"; "over 100 Myr" separates these remains from the next moss record.
items.section: Front matter: range.notes
items.evidence: Cardona-Correa reports 455–454 Ma deposits; repository boundaries place these in Sandbian. Ignatov relays the >100-million-year gap and age concerns.
items.source: [Cardona-Correa et al. 2016](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/full/10.1086/686242), full text; data/timescale.csv, read directly; [Ignatov and Maslova 2021](https://mapress.com/bde/article/download/bde.43.1.7/44441), indexed full-text passages.

items.claim: "Silurian and Early Devonian tubular microfossils" resemble Polytrichum calyptra hairs; "it is a resemblance, not a record".
items.section: Front matter: range.notes
items.evidence: Experimental calyptra residues resemble ancient tubes in morphology and wall dimensions; the authors propose possible moss origins, without establishing them.
items.source: [Kodner and Graham 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11250824/), abstract only.

items.claim: "moss crown at 380 (362-399) Ma ... or 488-602 Ma".
items.section: Front matter: range.notes
items.evidence: The review reports these numbers, including three Laenen estimates; Newton's original analysis and Laenen's relevant supplementary age table were inaccessible.
items.source: [Ignatov and Maslova 2021](https://www.mapress.com/bde/article/download/bde.43.1.7/44441/48190), indexed full-text introduction; [Laenen et al. 2014](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/267393141_Extant_diversity_of_bryophytes_emerged_from_successive_post-Mesozoic_diversification_bursts), main full text only, without the required supplement.

items.claim: "diverged 515-494 Ma"; bryophytes lost vasculature-associated genes; "hydroids are therefore a derived solution".
items.section: Affinity and controversies: Position
items.evidence: Harris supports the abstract's dates and inferred gene-family losses; these results alone do not establish the cellular evolutionary origin of hydroids.
items.source: [Harris et al. 2022](https://bpb-eu-w2.wpmucdn.com/blogs.bristol.ac.uk/dist/3/589/files/2022/09/Harris_et_al_2022.pdf), full text. Its main text gives 515–493 Ma.

items.claim: "Chosen to contrast: Water-transport, sporophyte-independence and height" against non-conducting Marchantia and tracheophytes.
items.section: Model transfer: Chosen to contrast
items.evidence: Sources distinguish hydroid-bearing moss gametophytes, complex thalloid liverworts lacking internal water-conducting cells, and xylem-bearing tracheophytes; moss sporophytes retain maternal dependence.
items.source: [Ligrone et al. 2012](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/221853422_Major_transitions_in_the_evolution_of_early_land_plants_a_bryological_perspective), full review; [Kubásek et al. 2021](https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/nph.17208), full primary study.

omissions: Kubásek studied P. commune, P. juniperinum and Polytrichastrum formosum directly. P. commune capsules have approximately 50 stomata, and stomatal sealing suppresses capsule gas exchange; the card unnecessarily leaves species-level sporophyte physiology unresolved. [Full primary text](https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/nph.17208).

Kubásek's corrected Table 3 reports P. commune capsule net assimilation of 0.09 µmol m−2 s−1 at 400 µmol mol−1 CO2, versus −0.35 after stomatal sealing, under saturating light. These are capsule-area rates, not lifetime carbon-autonomy fractions. The original online Table 3 duplicates Table 2 and must be replaced using the [full erratum](https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/nph.17473).

Kubásek distinguishes effectively homoiohydric developing sporophytes from poikilohydric gametophytes, while finding no stomatal conductance responses to light or CO2. Dependence, photosynthetic contribution and water regulation therefore need separate model variables. [Full primary text](https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/nph.17208).

The optical embolism metric measures cumulative changed image area. Refilling involved wetting both leaves and rhizome; the supplementary-video caption reports similar results in three samples despite the single illustrated time series. [Brodribb full text and supplementary description](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41477-020-0602-x).

Bippus discusses Polytrichopsida clock estimates of 297–471 Ma and questions their fossil calibration. Subtracting the family's first fossil from the whole-moss crown age does not measure the undocumented history of the hydroid lineage. [Full text](https://mihaibotany.online/pdf/BippusEtAl2017.pdf).

Cardona-Correa supplies multiple explicit arguments against modern contamination, including replicated extraction, matrix properties and chemical and morphological comparisons. These deserve representation alongside the later chronological-gap objection. [Full primary text](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/full/10.1086/686242).

Flora describes occasional stem forking and erect-to-decumbent stems, and flags taxonomic uncertainty around the elongated wetland form var. uliginosum. These qualify both branching='none' and transfer of maximum stem length as vertical stature. [Complete indexed Flora treatment](https://efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200002665).
model_transfer_assessment: The chosen contrast is useful: internal conduction, generation dominance and sporophyte dependence can be separated. Most hydraulic observations concern the named P. commune population, and the formosum distinction is handled carefully. However, microscopy, embolism area, conductance loss and refilling require separate model relationships; stem length is not automatically vertical height, and one species cannot establish a universal penalty for stomata-free tissue. The exclusions correctly address species, organs and sampling, but should incorporate the available P. commune capsule physiology and permit bounded functional analogy without implying ancestry.
overall: The card is substantially source-grounded, but needs revision before serving as a quantitative modelling reference. The principal problems are overly broad transfer recommendations, conflation of stem length with height, an unsupported universal claim about missing carbon fractions, and omission of directly relevant P. commune sporophyte measurements.
